Re: LD 1233 - An Act to Modify Confidentiality Laws to Protect Children Placed into Custody by the Department of Health and Human Services

Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services, thank you for the opportunity to provide information in opposition to LD 1233, An Act to Modify Confidentiality Laws to Protect Children Placed into Custody by the Department of Health and Human Services.

This bill would create a new mandatory disclosure provision within 22 MRSA �4008 that would require disclosure to "an agency or department involved in the placement of a child if a record of past substance use or domestic abuse by a person being considered for custody of the child exists."

OCFS is opposed to this bill as it represents an unnecessary statutory change. The title of the bill indicates the bill is intended to apply to placement of children who are in the Department's custody. OCFS already has access to all of our own records and utilizes those for the purpose of placing a child. The bill's language references "person being considered for custody", which is only relevant when considering adoption, otherwise children are placed in resource or kinship homes, but they remain in the Department's custody.

OCFS already reviews and considers its records as part of the licensing process for prospective resource parents, as well as for potential kinship placements. OCFS already has access to all of its own records and thus does not need a statutory mandatory disclosure provision and considers both past substance use and domestic violence, as well as any subsequent information or mitigating factors.

OCFS would urge the Committee to vote ought not to pass on LD 1233.

Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions during your deliberation of this bill.

Sincerely,

Bobbi L. Johnson, LMSW Director Office of Child and Family Services Maine Department of Health and Human Services
10042332:
Joan Petersen Swanville LD 1233
Dear Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and esteemed members of the Health and Human Services Committee, I write you in support of LD1233 as ought to pass. The abysmal record of child deaths while under the supervision of the Department of Human Services crys out for reform. Our children deserve every aide we can give them while under our care. You can improve the decision making process in the Department by allowing all testimony in the child placement process. Now there are instances of known prior domestic and/or substance abuse by an individual who is being considered for custody in which the testimony is prohibited due to confidentiality laws. This bill seeks redress and allows such testimony to be considered. Certainly the decision makers have critical thinking and discernment in determining the veracity of any and all testimony. If they are blind to all possible evidence via testimony, how can they make the best decision? I urge you to contemplate and make a decision to support the best outcomes for our children.
